question: How does substituent electronegativity and solvent polarity influence the conformational preferences of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone derivatives?
answer: The conformational preferences of 3-substituted N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone derivatives are influenced by both substituent electronegativity and solvent polarity. More electronegative substituents weaken hyperconjugative stabilization of the pseudo-axial (p-ax) conformation, making the pseudo-equatorial (p-eq) form more favorable, particularly in polar solvents. Solvent polarity shifts the equilibrium toward the p-eq conformation due to its larger dipole moment, while nonpolar environments favor the less polar p-ax form. Electronic structure calculations confirm that this behavior arises from competing hyperconjugation, steric repulsion, and electrostatic interactions, with solvation effects dominating in polar media.

The paper investigates the conformational preferences of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone (NMP) molecules substituted at the 3-position by methoxyl, thiomethoxyl, and selenomethoxyl groups.
